title: dutch-oven — pick the composition
question: Three compositions of the diner ticket-rail world for the main recipe surface. Which one carries forward — approve, combine, revise, or reject?

options.label: A. Rail on Top
options.thesis: The week's dinners clipped to a steel rail above a mustard hero; specials cards and a torn-ticket log below.
options.viewport: Full-width ticket rail with 4 day stubs; 'WHAT'S FOR DINNER?' headline; 3 menu-board recipe cards; 'LAST SERVED' ticket strip.
options.risk: Safest of the three; the rail is decoration unless the stubs are real interactive state.

options.label: B. Counter Pass
options.thesis: A stainless pass splits the screen: recipe library as a painted menu board above, your active and served tickets below.
options.viewport: Two-column menu board (MAINS / SIDES & SWEETS) with cook-time tags; steel pass holding ready tickets; 'YOUR TICKETS' log strip with SERVED stamps.
options.risk: Dense; the menu board must stay scannable with 20+ real recipes, not 8 pretty ones.

options.label: C. The Ticket Is the Page
options.thesis: The whole surface is one order dupe: tonight's recipe as line items with checkboxes, the queue and the log as perforated sections.
options.viewport: Full-bleed ticket: 'ORDER #042 — TONIGHT', dish name huge, ingredient checkbox line items, UP NEXT queue, SERVED count strip, bottle-cap nav on the right margin.
options.risk: Most radical; recipe discovery needs a second screen or the bottle-cap search must carry it.
